technical_and_design_decisions: All development will be done using Java 17 and Spring Framework 6.0 as the base platform.
Kafka source module will use the official Kafka client library and the Spring Kafka project for integration.
HDFS sink will use Hadoop FileSystem API, with syncable writes implemented via hflush() or hsync().
Custom module upload will be implemented as a Maven plugin and a Gradle plugin to allow automated builds and deployments.
Module versioning will be implemented by introducing a version field in the module descriptor and supporting version ranges in dependencies.
Certification against PHD 3.0 will involve setting up a test cluster running PHD 3.0 and running the existing Spring XD test suite, fixing any incompatibilities.
All new features will be designed to be backward-compatible with existing configuration, using optional flags.
The bug U1 will require investigation of the admin UI permission handling and shell command consistency; likely a misconfiguration or missing role mapping.
assumptions: The developer has full access to a development environment with Java 17, Maven, Gradle, Kafka, HDFS, and a PHD 3.0 cluster (or Docker images).
All user stories are independent and can be implemented sequentially, but effort estimation assumes they are done in a single increment.
Testing is done by the developer and includes unit tests, integration tests, and manual verification; automated CI/CD pipelines are available.
Documentation updates are limited to in-code comments, README files, and configuration reference.
No external dependencies beyond the already included libraries need to be added.
The bug U1 is a defect that can be reproduced and fixed within 3 days, including root cause analysis and testing.
The certification effort for U8 includes initial environment setup, test execution, and any required code changes to pass all tests on PHD 3.0.

activities.activity_description: Analyze all 8 user stories, define technical approach, and create design documents for the changes. Includes review of existing codebase and identification of affected modules.

activities.activity_name: Bug Fix for U1 - Role-based Error in Admin UI
activities.activity_description: Investigate the error occurring for ROLE_CREATE and ROLE_ADMIN when creating jobs from admin_ui, while shell works. Identify root cause (likely permission check or UI mapping), implement fix, and test both UI and shell workflows.

Add configuration option to specify the number of partitions for Kafka topic when creating or using the Kafka source module. Implement logic to partition payloads accordingly and ensure routing to intended consumer.

activities.activity_name: Dynamic Partition Subscription for Kafka Source (U3)
activities.activity_description: Implement ability for Kafka source module to dynamically subscribe to additional partitions at runtime. This may involve consumer rebalancing and partition assignment logic.

activities.activity_name: Syncable Writes Option for HDFS Sink (U4)
activities.activity_description: Add configuration flag to enable syncable writes (using hflush/hsync) on HDFS sink. Ensure data durability at cost of performance. Update documentation and add tests.

activities.activity_name: No Temporary Suffix Option for HDFS Sink (U5)
activities.activity_description: Add configuration option to disable the use of temporary .tmp suffix when writing files to HDFS. Instead write directly to the final filename. This complements the syncable writes feature. Implement and test.

activities.activity_name: Maven/Gradle Target for Custom Module Upload (U6)
activities.activity_description: Develop Maven plugin and Gradle plugin tasks to package and upload custom module fragments to a module repository. Ensure automated installation from build tools.
Add version metadata to custom modules, support version constraints in module descriptors, and implement upgrade/rollback logic. Update existing module loading mechanism.
Set up a test environment with PHD 3.0, run the full Spring XD test suite, identify and fix compatibility issues (e.g., API changes, dependencies). Update documentation for supported versions.
Perform end-to-end integration testing of all changes together. Identify and fix any cross-feature issues or regressions. Run automated test suites.
Update user guides, configuration reference, API documentation, and release notes to reflect all new features, options, and the bug fix.
Conduct self-review and refactoring of all code changes to ensure consistency, code quality, and adherence to project standards. Includes minor cleanup.
